<entry id="R00433">
<head-word>צִיץ</head-word>
<hw-number>II</hw-number>
<pos> m.</pos>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> preced.) </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>something glistening, foil</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Tanḥ. Vayetsé 12 (describing the Teraphim) מביאין … וכותבין על צ' זהב וכ' they get a firstborn man and slaughter him …, and write the name of a spirit of uncleanness on a golden plate, and put the plate under his tongue with sorcerous ceremonies &c.—Esp. 
<italic>the highpriest’s front plate</italic>. Succ. 5
<sup>a</sup> צ' דומה כמין טס וכ' the front plate was something like a gold foil &c.; Sabb. 63
<sup>b</sup>. Zeb. 88
<sup>b</sup> צ' … עזות פנים the plate procures forgiveness for sins committed by effrontery. Gen. R. s. 71 בזה צ' ובזה צ' in this (the tribe of Levi) is the sheen (of the high priest’s frontlet), and in that (the tribe of Judah) is the splendor (of the crown, Ps. CXXXII, 18); a. fr.—[
<plural-form>Pl. צִיצִין</plural-form>. Tosef. Sot. III, 4 ed. Zuck. בצ' with fineries, v. צִלְצוּל.]</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>blossom</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 53 (ref. to Is. XL, 8) יבש … ונבל צִיצוֹ the flower of Abimelech was dried up, and his blossom faded (his procreative faculty was lost); Yalk. Is. 309.—
<plural-form>Pl. צִיצִים, צִיצִין</plural-form>. Sabb. 145
<sup>b</sup> (ref. to Is. XXVII, 6) אלו … עושין צ' וכ' this refers to the scholars in Babylonia who create blossoms and flowers for the Torah (revive learning); a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>filament, thread, thread-like shred, fringe</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ib. 131
<sup>a</sup> Ms. M., v. צוּץ.—
<italic>Pl.</italic> as ab. Ib. 94
<sup>b</sup>; Tosef. ib. IX (X), 12 צפורן … וצ' וכ' a nail, and shreds (of skin) the largest portions of which are severed from the body. Sabb. XIX, 6 צ' המעכבין וכ' shreds of the corona which make the circumcision invalid. Y. ib. XIX, 17
<sup>a</sup>; a. fr.—Tosef. Ab. Zar. V (VI), 2 (describing a scarab or dragon used as an emblem of idolatry, v. דְּרָקוֹן) כל שהצ' יוצאין מצוארו from whose neck fringes come forth; Y. ib. III, 42
<sup>d</sup> top; Bab. ib. 43
<sup>a</sup></notes></sense></senses></entry>

<sense>

<italic>fringes</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gitt. 56
<sup>a</sup> שהיתה ציצתו נגררת וכ' the fringes of his cloak were dragged along on cushions. M. Kat. III, 4 תכלת לציצתו Y. ed. (Mish. a. Bab. ed. 19
<sup>a</sup> לציציתו; Rabb. D. S. quotes לציצתו) the blue thread for his show-fringes.—Kel. XVI, 4 סקורטיא … ויעשה את צִיצָתָהּ (Ar. ציציתיה, read: צִיצוֹתֶיהָ) a leather apron is considered finished, when … he attaches its fringes (cords); [Maim.: a leather table cloth …, when he puts on a 
<italic>bright center piece</italic>].—
<plural-form>Pl. צִיצוֹת,</plural-form> v. supra.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<pos> f.</pos>
<language-key>(b. h. </language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="unknown">צִיצִת; צוּץ</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> , v. 
<xref rid="R00229">צוּצִיתָא</xref>) </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>hair-lock</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Sifra Aḥăré, Par. 9, ch. XIII (ref. to Lev. XVIII, 3) שלא תגדל צ' that thou must not grow a lock (v. בְּלוּרִית). Zeb. 26
<sup>a</sup>; Yalk. Lev. 446 הוא בפנים וצִיצִיתוֹ וכ' if the sacrifice stands (within the sacred precincts), and its locks (prob. the tuft of its tail) are without.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>fringe</italic>, esp. 
<italic>the show-fringes</italic> (Num. XV, 38).</definition>
<notes> Sifré Num. 115 אין צ' אלא דבר היוצא ודבר כל שהוא by 
<italic>tsitsith</italic> is meant something that protrudes (hangs over) and is of a minute size; Men. 41
<sup>b</sup>. Sifré l. c. וצ' מן הגדילים, v. גְּדִילָה II. Men. 39
<sup>b</sup> פטורין מן הצ' require no show-fringes; חייבין בצ' require show-fringes; a. fr.—M. Kat. III, 4 (19
<sup>a</sup>), a. e., v. צִיצָה—
<plural-form>Pl. צִיצִיּוֹת</plural-form>. Men. 44
<sup>a</sup> באו ארבע צִיצִיּוֹתָיו וכ' the four fringes of his garment came into sight and slapped him in the face (reproached him for his sensuality, reminding him of Num. XV, 39). Sifré l. c.; Men. III, 7 ארבע צ' מעכבות וכ' the four fringes are dependent on one another, v. עָכַב. Ib. 43
<sup>a</sup> אין … עד שיתיר צִיצִיּוֹתֶיהָ you must not sell a fringed cloak to a gentile without removing its show-fringes; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="R00450">
<head-word>צִיר</head-word>
<hw-number>II</hw-number>
<pos> m.</pos>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="A00083"> צוּר)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>hinge, pivot</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Men. 33
<sup>a</sup>; Erub. 11
<sup>b</sup> היכר צ', v. אַבְקָתָא. Kel. XI, 2; Num. R. s. 12, v. פּוֹתָה. Erub. X, 12 מחזירין צ' התחתון you may bring back to its socket the lower pivot (of a door of a chest &c.). Yoma 39
<sup>b</sup> וצ' דלתות וכ' the turning hinges of the Temple door were heard &c.; a. fr.—

<sense>
<definition> v.

<italic>polished buckler</italic> or 
<italic>cuirass</italic> (cmp. סַנְוַורְתָּא).</definition>
<notes> Midr. Till. to Ps. I מנין … ת"ל וכ' whence do we learn to include the fourth side (as protected)? We read (Ps. V, 13) ‘as with a cuirass &c.’ Ib. to Ps. XXXV, 2 וכי למגן וצ' וכ' (ed. Ps. 842; Tanḥ. Naso 23. Ex. R. s. 40 (ref. to צנן, Josh. XV, 37) [read:] צנן שהוא צ' Jerusalem is surnamed Zenan, because it is a cuirass (the Temple being a protection); a. e.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<sup>d</sup> קורדום … לא צ' ועצי זית if one finds an axe, he may use it for chopping ordinary wood, but not for stone-palms and olive trees; Tosef. ib. II, 22 צנם ed. Zuck. <entry id="R00609">
<head-word>צִנָּה</head-word>
<head-word>צִינָּה</head-word>
<hw-number>III</hw-number>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="A00083"> צָנַן)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>cold</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Tosef. Ohol. II, 6 נכנסה עליו צ' ומת he caught cold on it (on the trepanned skull) and died. Y. Sabb. XIV, 14
<sup>c</sup> bot. תשעים … מתים בצ' וכ' ninety-nine men die from cold to one by the hands of heaven; Lev. R. s. 16. B. Mets. 107
<sup>b</sup> (ref. to כל חלי, Deut. VII, 15) זו צ' that means cold. Tosef. Sabb. III (IV), 5 צִינָּתָן; Y. ib. III, 6
<sup>b</sup> top צִינָּתָהּ, v. פּוּג h.; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. צִנִּים, צִנִּין, צִי'</plural-form>. Y. B. Kam. VIII, beg. 6
<sup>b</sup> הטיל עליו שלג או צ' וכ' if he put snow or ice-cold water &c.; ib. bot. צונן. Ex. R. s. 25, beg. בקש צ' … בקש חמים וכ' (not גחלים) if he wants ice-water, he gets it (out of the 
<italic>milliarium</italic>); if he wants hot water &c.; (Tanḥ. Vayera 10 חמין … צונן).—צ' פחים (adopted from Prov. XXII, 5) 
<italic>blowing cold winds, cold draughts</italic>; [oth. opin.: צ' ופ' 
<italic>cold and heat</italic>, v. פַּח II]. B. Mets. l. c.; Ab. Zar. 3
<sup>b</sup>; Keth. 30
<sup>a</sup>; B. Bath. 144
<sup>b</sup> הכל בידי שמים חוץ מצ' פ' everything is in the power of heavens (comes from no fault of man), except sickness from cold droughts, as we read (Prov. l. c.) &c.; Yalk. Prov. 960 מצ' ופ'.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="R00611">

<xref rid="A00083"> צָנַע)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>retired, discreet, chaste, decorous</italic>.</definition>
<notes>
<pgbrk id="pg1291" />Nidd. 12
<sup>a</sup> כל … נקרא צ' he who fulfils the words of the scholars is called discreet (pious). Y. Dem. VI, 25
<sup>d</sup> top (ref. to צְנוּעֵי Mish. ib. 6) שהכשר נקרא צ' the worthy man is called 
<italic>tsanuʿa</italic>. Ber. 62
<sup>a</sup> צ' בבית הכסא decent in his manners in the privy. Ib. צ' באורחותיו decorous in his ways; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. צְנוּעִים, צְנוּעִין</plural-form>. Cant. R. to VI, 6 (ref. to רחלים ib.) מה רחל זו צנועה כן היו ישראל צ' וכ' as the lamb is pure, so were the Israelites pure and virtuous in the Midianitic war. Dem. VI, 6 צְנוּעֵי בית הלל, v. כָּשֵׁר II. Maas. Sh. V, 1 הצ' מניחין וכ' the conscientious lay money aside &c.; a. fr.—
<italic>Fem.</italic> צְנוּעָה. Sabb. 53
<sup>b</sup> כמה צ' אשה זו how chaste was this woman! Cant. R. l. c., v. supra; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. צְנוּעוֹת</plural-form>. Keth. 2
<sup>b</sup>, sq. משום צ' for the sake of the virtuous women, opp. פרוּצות. Nidd. 12
<sup>a</sup>, v. עֵד; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

Dehr. צני') the hook of an earring (detached) is clean; Tosef. ib. B. Mets. I, 9 [read:] צ' של נזם (v. R. S. to Kel. l. c.). Ib. III, 7 ניטל … מפני הצ' (ed. Zuck. הצינורות) if the flat portion of the baker’s shovel is broken off, it is susceptible to uncleanness on account of the hook on the other end (used as a poker); ניטלה הצ' (ed. Zuck. הצינורת) if the curved end is broken off (v. קַלִּיגְרָפוֹן). Yoma 12
<sup>a</sup> מהפך בצ' he turns (a piece of flesh &c. on the altar) with the hook. Tosef. Sabb. VIII (IX), 16 כדי לעשות צ' קטנה enough coal to forge a small hook; ib. IX (X), 5 כדי … ממנו צ' וכ' enough iron to make of it &c. Men. 107
<sup>a</sup>; Sabb. 90
<sup>a</sup> צ' וכ' a small bronze hook. Gen. R. s. 74 אפי' מחט אפי' צ' וכ' thou hast not found with me even a pin or a hook (of thine); a. fr.—[Num. R. s. 8, v. next w.]—

<sup>b</sup>, sq. מחטין וצ' pins (or needles) and hooks; a. e.—Chald., v. צִנּוֹרָא I.</notes></sense></senses></entry>
